By "night time shift", I assume you mean late-nights or overnights. While I've never worked for Amazon, here's my experience with working those sort of hours:
·Peaceful commutes. The traffic, even in the city, is a fraction of what it is in the daytime, and it's really rather pleasant compared to sitting at yet another light, hoping the 20 cars in front of you leave you enough yellow to not be late for work
·Horrible experiences getting government/etc type errands done. When everything shuts down at 4:30pm, and you don't wake up until 8pm, you better get used to staying up late after work, to get to city hall or whatever first thing in the morning, and then sit there waiting behind all the morning people, before you can finally get to bed for a few hours.
·Neighbors don't care when you sleep. Can't sleep through your neighbor mowing his lawn at noon? Has the gas company being doing road-work on your street for 2 solid weeks now? Welcome to Nobody-Caresville. They will start at 6am, and you will learn earplugs only help so much.
·Shopping is either way easier or way harder. Live near a 24-hour store? Welcome to no lines, no crowds, and peaceful, pensive thoughts about what to have for supper. Your stores close by 9pm? Better hope you stocked up on your last days off, because they'll be your next chance to buy more of whatever you ran out of.
·Family don't care when you sleep. Kids? Parents? Roommates? They are all just as dumbfounded by the idea that 10am is a bad time to wake you up over something retarded. They will even blame you for not conforming better, if you get angry over the lack of sleep.
·Easier job, better pay. Most jobs, especially of the major corporation variety, have a nighttime pay differential. You can get as much as 10-20% more than your dayshift counterparts, and not have to worry as much about all the hustle and bustle that happens during normal business hours. Please note that warehouse jobs like Amazon probably take advantage of this second point, and have you do the majority of the stocking/reshelving/etc type jobs that would get backed-up throughout the day.

That covers most of the basic things, I think. Hope it helps your decision! Amazon is pretty well-known for working its employees extra-hard, but it would also look pretty nice on a resume at a future, less slave-driving type company later on.
